newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps all lower, some sellers holding bac.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps all lower, some sellers holding bac.

text.p: European oil swaps fell on Tuesday as U.S oil futures headed resolutely lower just after the open.
Sellers became increasingly reluctant as the day progressed with dealers commenting that an 75/80 cent drop in frontmonth NYMEX crude and Brent was overdone.
Brent crude CFDs dropped by up to 10 cents on further out weeks, while fuel, gasoline and naphtha lost $2.00 a tonne and more.
Shell cut runs at its Pernis, Rotterdam unit by about 14 percent, echoing similar cuts at Texaco and BP's Nerefco complex last week, a supportive move for the market.
Brent CFDs eased back with May 27-30 hunkered down at 4.00 cents over July compared with 7.5 cents over on Friday when a very high dated Brent cargo (July +17 cents) lifted the market.

On Tuesday the same buyer of Friday's cargo entered the market and took another dated Brent at a more modest +9 cents. Some dealers said they saw the strong numbers as an attempt to support a long CFD position, citing the hefty backwardation for further out weeks.
June 2-6 eased down to around -25 cents against Brent from -16 cents on Friday, while June 27 to July 13 collapsed to -25 cents from -13 cents. Two June 18-24 CFDs were done at August -30 cents.
High sulphur fuel was $2.00 a tonne weaker with $81.00 and $81.50 done for June while July was pegged around $83-84 although both contracts had been 50 cents or so weaker earlier in the day.
Low sulphur, though quiet, was unable to resist the draw down and June was pegged around $94.50 and July at $93.50.

Gasoline saw a fair degree of activity early, but business dried up once the U.S led drop materialised as sellers started to flake amid expectations of a correction to the drop sometime later this week.
Physical barges were done at $204 and June swaps went at $204, $205 and $205.25. The June crack was also done at $5.37.
Naptha was sharply lower, dropping up to $2.50 a tonne with July thought concluded at $188.75.
